thumbnail.title: Divisibility by 9 & 11
thumbnail.subtitle: Digit Sum & Alternating Sum — 10 Second Trick
highlights: Both rules tested on all 4 options

youtube.title: Divisibility by 9 & 11 Trick | Number System | RRB SSC Railway Banking
youtube.description:
Learn the fastest shortcut to check divisibility by 9 and 11.

Rule of 9: Add all digits — if divisible by 9, number is divisible by 9.
Rule of 11: Alternating digit sum — if result is 0 or divisible by 11, number passes.

This question is from RRB 2024 exam paper.

question.text: Which of the following numbers is divisible completely by both 9 and 11?
question.audio: Which of the following numbers is divisible completely by both nine and eleven? The number must pass the Rule of Nine and the Rule of Eleven. Both tests must be satisfied.

scenes.text: Which of the following numbers is divisible completely by both 9 and 11?
scenes.audio: Which of the following numbers is divisible completely by both nine and eleven? The number must pass two tests — the Rule of Nine and the Rule of Eleven. Both must be satisfied at the same time.

Option A, two lakh seventy seven thousand two hundred and eighteen. Option B, ten thousand and ninety eight. Option C, twelve thousand three hundred and forty five. Option D, one lakh eighty one thousand nine hundred and ninety eight. Pause and think which one passes both rules.

steps.audio: The Rule of Nine is very simple. Add all the digits of the number. If the total is divisible by nine, the number is also divisible by nine. For example, eighteen divided by nine is two exactly. So any number whose digit sum is eighteen is divisible by nine.

render.text: Rule of 9 → Add all digits → sum ÷ 9 = 0 remainder → Divisible ✓

steps.audio: The Rule of Eleven uses alternating plus and minus signs. Starting from the left, assign plus to the first digit, minus to the second, plus to the third, and so on. If the final result is zero or divisible by eleven, the number passes. This is the fastest shortcut.

render.heading: Rule of 11
items: Assign alternating + − + − signs from left digit
If result = 0 or divisible by 11 → Divisible ✓

steps.audio: Let us test Option A, which is two lakh seventy seven thousand two hundred and eighteen. We will apply both rules.
Checking Option A now.
The six digits are two, seven, seven, two, one, eight.
Digit sum: two plus seven plus seven plus two plus one plus eight equals twenty seven. Twenty seven divided by nine is three. Rule of Nine — passes.

Alternating sum: plus two, minus seven, plus seven, minus two, plus one, minus eight. That is two minus seven is minus five, plus seven is two, minus two is zero, plus one is one, minus eight is minus seven. Minus seven is not zero and not divisible by eleven. Option A FAILS Rule of Eleven.
Now Option B, ten thousand and ninety eight. This has only five digits — let us check quickly.
Checking Option B.
The five digits are one, zero, zero, nine, eight.
Digit sum: one plus zero plus zero plus nine plus eight equals eighteen. Eighteen divided by nine is exactly two. Rule of Nine — passes.

Alternating sum: plus one, minus zero, plus zero, minus nine, plus eight. One minus zero is one, plus zero is one, minus nine is minus eight, plus eight is zero. The result is zero! Zero is divisible by eleven. Option B passes both rules.
Option C, twelve thousand three hundred and forty five. Let us check the Rule of Nine first.
Checking Option C.
Digit sum: one plus two plus three plus four plus five equals fifteen. Fifteen divided by nine gives remainder six. Option C FAILS Rule of Nine immediately. No need to check Rule of Eleven.
Option D, one lakh eighty one thousand nine hundred and ninety eight. It has six digits.
Checking Option D.
The six digits are one, eight, one, nine, nine, eight.
Digit sum: one plus eight plus one plus nine plus nine plus eight equals thirty six. Thirty six divided by nine is four exactly. Rule of Nine — passes.

Alternating sum: plus one, minus eight, plus one, minus nine, plus nine, minus eight. One minus eight is minus seven, plus one is minus six, minus nine is minus fifteen, plus nine is minus six, minus eight is minus fourteen. Minus fourteen is not zero and not divisible by eleven. Option D FAILS.

Only Option B, ten thousand and ninety eight, passes both the Rule of Nine and the Rule of Eleven. Digit sum eighteen is divisible by nine, and alternating sum zero is divisible by eleven. The correct answer is Option B.
